# TapTalk

> TapTalk is a free, open-source (MIT), 100 percent on-device dictation app for macOS on Apple Silicon. Hold a key and speak (or press it once to start and again to finish), and the transcript is pasted into any app. Speech recognition runs on the Apple Neural Engine; nothing is sent to a server unless the user explicitly enables the optional OpenAI cloud engine with their own key.

## Key facts

- Price: free. No subscription, no trial, no account, no word limits.
- License: MIT. Source: https://github.com/vakharwalad23/tap-talk
- Platform: macOS 14 or later, any Apple Silicon Mac. Newer chips have a faster Neural Engine, so newer Macs are faster. Version 0.7.0.
- Install: brew install --cask vakharwalad23/tap/taptalk, or the .dmg from GitHub Releases.
- Privacy: audio is processed in memory on-device and discarded. No telemetry, no analytics, no crash reporting. An optional daily update check asks GitHub for the latest version; it stays off until you say yes.
- Speech models (downloaded at runtime, never bundled): Orukeet r3 (default for new installs; English and 24 European languages, auto-detected; about 15 percent fewer word errors than Parakeet across 25 FLEURS languages, and about as fast on Apple M3 Pro, both near 0.1 s key-up-to-paste; CC-BY-SA-4.0), NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (fallback, and the base for optional live typing; English and European, auto-detected), NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR Multilingual 0.6B (Hindi, Marathi, Urdu, Chinese, Japanese and more), NVIDIA Parakeet Realtime EOU 120M (optional live typing). Existing Parakeet users get a one-time in-app prompt to upgrade to Orukeet; Parakeet is always kept as the fallback and for live typing.
- Key mode: Hold to talk (default) or Press to toggle, set in Settings. Esc or the cross on the floating pill cancels a recording; the tick finishes it. Using the dictation key in a shortcut (for example Right Cmd plus C) does not start a recording. If the Mac locks or sleeps mid-dictation, the text is kept in the app instead of being pasted.
- Smart Mode: an optional second hotkey rewrites the transcript with a local LLM (Qwen 2.5 1.5B via llama.cpp) to remove filler, resolve spoken corrections, and match the app being typed into. Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI) are supported.
- Hinglish: Hindi dictation can be output as Roman-script Hinglish, on-device.
- Microphone: when Bluetooth headphones are the default input and the lid is open, TapTalk records with the Mac's built-in microphone, so the headphones keep high-quality playback while dictating.
- Built with SwiftUI and Rust (no Electron). Models are memory-mapped; about 164 MB resident with a model loaded.
- Not yet notarized by Apple; the Homebrew cask clears the Gatekeeper quarantine flag.

## Compared with alternatives

TapTalk is a free, open-source, on-device alternative to Wispr Flow (cloud only, subscription), superwhisper (best models cloud or paid, account required), MacWhisper (closed source, paid Pro), VoiceInk (open source but the prebuilt app is paid, GPLv3), Handy (free and MIT, but a Tauri web UI with no Neural Engine use and no built-in AI rewrite), and Apple Dictation (no AI cleanup, fixed model).
